subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Indirect Reciprocity
description: A fast breakdown of Indirect Reciprocity for builders.

hook.text: You help a stranger. A different stranger helps you later. You never met, but your reputation traveled ahead of you.

buildup.text: Indirect reciprocity: I help you, someone else helps me. It works through reputation networks and the spread.

discovery.text: Nowak showed indirect reciprocity sustains cooperation in large groups where direct repeated interaction is unlikely.

twist.text: Online reviews are an indirect reciprocity system. You review for strangers; strangers review for you.

climax.text: In a connected world, every interaction can be observed. Your reputation extends far beyond those you deal.

punchline.text: Help someone and the help comes back from someone else.

quiz.question: How does indirect reciprocity sustain cooperation?
options: Through reputation networks that reward helpful behavior from third parties

details.summary: Indirect reciprocity occurs when people help strangers because their cooperative behavior builds a good reputation that attracts future help from others, creating a system where cooperation spreads through reputation rather than direct exchange.
details.whyItMatters: Indirect reciprocity explains large-scale cooperation among strangers in societies too large for repeated direct interaction. Reputation systems, online reviews, and social credit all leverage this mechanism.
takeaways: Helping strangers builds reputation that attracts future cooperation
Reputation tracking enables cooperation beyond direct relationships
Online review systems are modern implementations of indirect reciprocity

faq.question: How does indirect reciprocity differ from direct reciprocity?
faq.answer: Direct reciprocity is I help you because you helped me. Indirect reciprocity is I help you because others will see my helpfulness and help me later. The cooperation is mediated by reputation rather than direct exchange.

faq.question: Why does reputation sustain cooperation?
faq.answer: People with good reputations receive more help and better treatment. This payoff for being cooperative makes it individually rational to help strangers. The system collapses if reputation tracking breaks down.
